record.original_question: For a finite group G, let χ1(G) denote the totality of the degrees of all irreducible complex characters of G with allowance for their multiplicities. Suppose that H is a finite group with χ1(H) = χ1(G). a) If G is an almost simple group, must H be isomorphic to G? b) If G is a quasisimple group, must H be isomorphic to G? This is true if G is a simple group(see 11.8(a) in Archive).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite group $G$, let $\chi_1(G)$ denote the multiset of degrees of all irreducible complex characters of $G$ (each degree counted with its multiplicity, i.e. the number of irreducible characters of that degree). Equivalently, $\chi_1(G)$ encodes the isomorphism type of the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}G$ as a direct sum of matrix algebras.

Recall that a finite group $G$ is called:
- almost simple if there exists a non-abelian finite simple group $S$ with $S \trianglelefteq G \leq \mathrm{Aut}(S)$;
- quasisimple if $G$ is perfect (i.e. $G = [G,G]$) and the quotient $G/Z(G)$ is a non-abelian finite simple group.

It is known that every non-abelian finite simple group $G$ is determined up to isomorphism by $\chi_1(G)$: that is, for every finite group $H$ with $\chi_1(H) = \chi_1(G)$, one has $H \cong G$.

Decide whether the same uniqueness statement holds in each of the following two settings:

(a) If $G$ is a finite almost simple group and $H$ is a finite group with $\chi_1(H) = \chi_1(G)$, must $H \cong G$?

(b) If $G$ is a finite quasisimple group and $H$ is a finite group with $\chi_1(H) = \chi_1(G)$, must $H \cong G$?
artifact.status_search_result: The simple-group case (Question 11.8(a) of the Kourovka Notebook) is established: every non-abelian finite simple group is determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of its irreducible complex character degrees. For quasisimple groups, results of Nguyen, Tong-Viet and others show that every quasisimple group except possibly some covers of alternating groups (and a couple of small exceptions like 3·PSL3(4), 6·PSU4(3)) is determined by its complex group algebra, so part (b) is largely but not completely settled. The almost simple case (a) has been verified for many families (e.g. results on almost simple groups of Lie type and on alternating/sporadic groups), but the general statement is still considered open in the Kourovka problem list.

status_evidence.title: Characterizing Finite Quasisimple Groups by Their Complex Group Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: every quasisimple group except covers of the alternating groups is uniquely determined up to isomorphism by its complex group algebra
status_evidence.claim: Part (b) for quasisimple groups is settled in most cases, with covers of alternating groups remaining.

status_evidence.title: Alternating and Sporadic Simple Groups are Determined by Their Character Degrees
status_evidence.snippet: alternating groups, sporadic simple groups, and the Tits group are determined by their character degrees
status_evidence.claim: The simple-group base case (Kourovka 11.8(a)) is solved.

status_evidence.title: Recognition of finite quasi-simple groups by the degrees of their irreducible representations
status_evidence.snippet: quasisimple classical group L is uniquely determined up to isomorphism by the structure of its complex group algebra when L/Z(L) is not isomorphic to PSL3(4) or PSU4(3)
status_evidence.claim: Quasisimple classical groups are determined by their complex group algebras with limited exceptions.
